thread:
mariam: Heads up — we're seeing a spike of dropped pod connections in eu-west1 GPU pool, multiple services reporting RSTs and 502s. Datadog alert came in ~3m ago. Possible conntrack/NAT exhaustion. @sre-oncall can you triage?

Datadog-bot: ALERT: conntrack_usage > 90% on nodes: gpu-eu-west1-*-pool (avg 92%). Link: https://app.datadoghq.com/alerts/12345678

alex: Which nodes exactly? any kernel logs / dmesg showing conntrack overflow?

cheng: Jumping in — I grabbed one node: `ssh gpu-eu-west1-03` then: 
```
cat /proc/sys/net/netfilter/nf_conntrack_count
# => 245760
cat /proc/sys/net/netfilter/nf_conntrack_max
# => 262144
```
Looks very close to max. Also see a bunch of `nf_conntrack: table full, dropping packet` in `dmesg`.

raj: Quick mitigation: bump nf_conntrack_max and reduce timeouts for established TCP connections. E.g.:
```
sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=524288
sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_tcp_timeout_established=180
sysctl -w net.ipv4.ip_local_port_range=\"10240 65535\"
```
We can push via a DaemonSet that runs `sysctl` until nodes reboot.

mariam: Ok do that as emergency patch if you think it’ll stop the drops. What's the root cause in the medium term?

cheng: Preliminary cause: a lot of east-west egress from GPU pods to internal redis/feature-store, many short-lived outbound connections (bursty jobs). Each outgoing connection creates a SNAT conntrack entry on the node that handles SNAT, so bursts blow trough conntrack. Also ephemeral port reuse looks constrained.

alex: Could this be exacerbated by kube-proxy iptables mode vs ipvs? iptables creates more NAT churn. Are these clusters iptables or ipvs?

cheng: We're on iptables for that pool. We saw higher conntrack churn in iptables clusters historically. Switching to IPVS could help, but that's a medium effort.

raj: Longer-term options:
- move services to long-lived pooled connections (connection pooling) instead of short lived TCPs
- increase conntrack kernel limits via node image / sysctl defaults (persistent)
- move kube-proxy to IPVS in this pool
- consider a SNAT gateway (NAT instance) design so SNAT load is off node local conntrack tables
- consider enabling `externalTrafficPolicy: Local` where applicable to avoid SNAT for LB traffic

mariam: For short term, @sre-oncall please apply the `nf_conntrack_max` bump + ephemeral port range change to the affected node pool and monitor. Also set up a rollback plan (revert sysctl to previous).

sre-oncall: Will do. Applying DaemonSet patch now to set sysctl values across gpu-eu-west1 nodes. I'll post logs.

Datadog-bot: NOTE: alert suppressed for 5m for gpu-eu-west1 pool by sre-oncall

alex: After bump, can we also lower TCP ESTABLISHED timeout a bit to shrink table retention? 180s is fine for testing.

cheng: Agreed. Also adding a quick metric: `conntrack_creates_per_minute` on nodes to see churn rate. If creates >> max/retention we need app changes or central SNAT.

raj: Also double-check `net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_tcp_timeout_time_wait` and `tcp_fin_timeout` for improvement. But test carefully — lowering timeouts can affect legitimate long connections.

mariam: Noted. I'm creating INC ticket and will track follow-up: INC-20260318-42. Please add proposed remediation items and owners. We'll schedule postmortem if we get recurring alerts in 7d.

cheng: Quick note — one of the user-facing services is starting 1000 short-lived workers per job which opens outbound to feature-store; engineering to look at pooling.

alex: Thanks, team. Ping me if any nodes still show `table full` after the sysctl rollout.

sre-oncall: Sysctl DS applied across 8 nodes, values set. Monitoring. Early signs: conntrack_count dropped from ~245k to ~60k on node an hour after change (connections aged out). Still keeping alerting at 85% to watch.

mariam: Great. Postmortem and remediation plan due EOD tomorrow.

cheng: I'll open a PR for connection pooling and add a note to the deployment runbook about conntrack limits.

raj: I'll draft a follow-up RFC describing SNAT gateway and IPVS migration options.

mariam: Thanks all. :thumbsup:
